claims.text: The as-cast WMoNbTi alloy has an average grain size of approximately 50 µm.
The as-cast WMoNbTi alloy has a yield strength of approximately 1.0 GPa.
The as-cast WMoNbTi alloy has a uniform elongation of approximately 2%.
The as-cast WMoNbTi alloy has an ignition-threshold velocity of approximately 450 m/s.
High-pressure torsion can refine this alloy to an average grain size below 500 nm.
Submicron grain refinement increases grain-boundary density.
Hall–Petch strengthening from the refined grains raises the yield stress.
A high density of grain boundaries impedes strain localization in the WMoNbTi alloy.
The increased grain-boundary density promotes more homogeneous dislocation activity.
More homogeneous dislocation activity extends uniform deformation and improves room-temperature ductility.
Under dynamic loading, the fine-grained structure partitions deformation into multiple micro-shear bands.
The multiple micro-shear bands generate sufficient adiabatic heating to preserve impact-induced ignition.
After high-pressure torsion, the alloy will have a yield strength of at least 1.2 GPa.
After high-pressure torsion, the alloy will have a uniform elongation of at least 10%.
After high-pressure torsion, the ignition-threshold velocity will remain within 10% of 450 m/s.
Grain refinement will improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing impact-induced energy release.
The proposed behavior applies at room temperature for grain sizes from 0.1 to 1 µm and strain rates from 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The predicted uniform elongation is at least 10% from a 2% baseline, but the experiment only falsifies failure to gain 5 percentage points; an outcome between 7% and 10% would miss the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The predicted yield strength is at least 1.2 GPa, whereas the falsification rule permits any result that does not decrease by more than 10%; many results below 1.2 GPa would fail the quantitative prediction but not falsify the hypothesis.
